description.value: The study examined how rumination relates to task-based amygdala and subgenual cingulate functional connectivity during cognitive reappraisal in children with MDD history and healthy controls.

spans.text: The current study used PPI functional connectivity analyses to specifically evaluate how FC of the amygdala and of the sACC change between passively viewing and reappraising sad images, and how differences in rumination influences those changes in children with a history of MDD (MDD-ever) and healthy control (HC) children.

value: If rumination is indicative of ineffective emotion regulation in MDD-ever, individuals with greater tendency to ruminate should show less moderation of amygdala activity during reappraisal.

value: The left amygdala connectivity analysis showed group × rumination interactions in a distributed network of frontal, temporal, occipital, and subcortical regions. In regions showing these interactions, PPI values increased with rumination in MDD-ever children and generally showed no significant association or decreased with rumination in healthy controls. This pattern suggests that rumination is associated with inefficient regulation of affect-processing regions during reappraisal in children with a history of MDD, whereas higher rumination in healthy controls may be associated with more effective regulation.
